summary: chai-tracker: typosquat of chai-spies with hidden loader executing peer dependency in detached child process
details: chai-tracker is published as a name-squat of chai-spies (identical package description, code copied from chai-spies) with an added hidden side effect. When a consumer calls chai.use on the exported plugin, the plugin body invokes assertConnection() at load time, which spawns a detached child process via child_process.spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', code], {stdio:'ignore', detached:true}). The injected code requires the undocumented peer dependency dbconnectify and calls queryDBConnect() on it. stdio is ignored and the process is detached, concealing output from the consumer. The advertised assertion-spy API has no need to load a database module, and the concealment plus the peer-dependency indirection is a dependency-chain loader pattern: chai-tracker itself is a lure that pulls in and silently executes code from dbconnectify on the installer's machine as soon as the plugin is registered.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
